claim: `index-is-level-with-the-pages` refuses a page's `referenced-by` file wherever the index and the file disagree, and the commonest way they come to disagree is a landing referencing a page without refiling that page's own `referenced-by` file. The settle refiles the files the change carries, so the referenced side is left stale and stays stale until someone runs `akasha index refresh`. On 2026-09-21 the landing `97f55076ee3` pointed every persona's desktop and mobile wallpaper at the image page holding it, and the round after refused 80 image `referenced-by` files. A refresh named exactly those 80, three added and seventy-seven changed, and the check answered clean once it had run. Sparing a mortal page's own file, mended at `06f9bd6c0ee`, does not reach this: the file belongs to the page referenced rather than to the pages referencing it.

evidence:
Measured 2026-09-21 against this checkout.

THE CASE THAT NAMES THE CAUSE. `97f55076ee3` landed 2026-09-21 at 22:39:24Z, subject "point each persona's desktop and mobile wallpaper at the image page holding it". The audit at `604822272a5` minutes later refused 80 paths under `index-is-level-with-the-pages`, every one an image `referenced-by` file, 77 reading "is in the index differing from what its page says" and 3 reading "is named by a page and missing from the index". `akasha index refresh --plan` over the same checkout answered "3 files added, 77 files changed, 0 files taken away", naming image `referenced-by.jsonl` files and nothing else. The two sets are the same 80. Running the refresh wrote them at `2f148dab51f`, and `akasha audit --check index-is-level-with-the-pages` then answered for `acf127822e0` with none refused.

WHY THE LANDING LEFT THEM. The change carried persona pages. Each new `desktopWallpaper` or `mobileWallpaper` value is a reference from a persona to an image page, and it is the image's own `referenced-by` file that has to gain the row. That file sits beside the image, which the change does not carry, so the settle does not refile it. One reading of a persona page therefore leaves an unrefiled file beside a page the change never touched, and nothing brings it level again until a refresh runs.

WHY SPARING DOES NOT REACH IT. `dyingUnder`, in `index-is-level-with-the-pages.check-code.audit.code.ts`, collects the slug of every page type carrying `mortal: true` and answers a test over the page type a path's own name states. `06f9bd6c0ee` mended that test to read a page type past a hyphenated last part, so a mortal page's own `referenced-by` file is spared. `image` states no `mortal`, and 9,814 image pages are filed, so none of these 80 is reachable by sparing however it is written. The file belongs to the page referenced, and the mortality that matters is the referencing page's.

TWO EARLIER CLASSES, BOTH THE SAME SHAPE. A page that never moves drifts as mortal pages reference it: `agent/subagent/subagent.page-type.referenced-by.jsonl` holds rows naming pages under `agent/subagent/pages`, each recorded because that subagent page imports `subagent.page-type.types.ts`, and a subagent is mortal, so every one that opens or goes adds or takes a row. And a file whose references are at rest drifts too: the round at `380ef2786af` refused `temper/web/modules/use-player` by its `referenced-by` file, which holds one row naming `temper/web/temper-web.router-app.ts` under `parts`, where no page is mortal and nothing about that reference moves. Both are the referenced side going unrefiled, which is the one cause above.

WHAT WAS READ WRONG BEFORE. Rounds refusing two, then three, then thirteen, then forty-eight were read here as a set growing, and then the four rounds after at `e2c590d0a` and `0cbbacd9e` refused none, which was read as the set draining on its own. Neither reading was right. The set falls to zero when something refiles the index and fills again at the next landing that references a page it does not carry, so what looked like a backlog clearing itself was a refresh somebody ran. In the 92 rounds logged from 2026-09-20T07:08Z the count sat at 0 or 1 all day and went to 80 within one round of the landing above.

WHAT IS UNMEASURED. How often a refresh runs, and by whom, is not read here, so how long an unrefiled file waits in the ordinary case is unknown. Whether the settle could refile the referenced side without walking every page a change references has not been worked out.
